=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired leaves at a single node visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear grouped near the stem apex, with short internodes)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without distinct leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaves are oval with rounded ends, widest near the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip is pointed but not sharply tapered)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is blunt and curved)

    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles are round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem is firm, green with some bark, typical of young woody plant)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green with brown patches (stem is primarily green, with areas of brownish bark or lichen)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth, no ridges or lenticels visible)

    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex visible when stems or leaves are damaged)
